answer: Under geological-rate trust decay, each identity pays an admission fee of copper coins equal to 10×2^(n−1), where n counts prior mints from the same device fingerprint: the first costs 10 copper, the tenth 5120. Honest agents minting once per decade pay 10, while a comet-swarm attacker wanting 100 identities pays over 5 million total, and slow decay makes duplicates worthless over long years. Each applicant also binds a terrace attestation key to one hardware chip, so a single chip cannot honestly onboard more than a few identities before its fees explode.
